sections.h2: Who bills property tax inside Columbia city limits?
sections.html:
Two governments bill a Columbia homeowner: the City of Columbia and Maury County. The city's Property Tax page says anyone living inside the city limits must pay both the city and the county tax.

The Maury County Property Assessor appraises the property, and the Maury County Trustee collects county tax at One Public Square in Columbia. The Assessor works from 6 Public Square and answers at 931-375-4001, while the Trustee takes calls at 931-375-2201, Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 4 p.m.

County notices are addressed to whoever owned the parcel on January 1. Tennessee law does not require the mailing of notices, so a missing bill does not excuse payment or waive interest.

sections.h2: When does Columbia city property tax come due, and is the window open now?
sections.html:
City tax is payable without penalty from November 1 through December 15. Today is November 15, 2026, so the window is open and closes in a month.

After December 15 the city adds charges in steps:

  • 0.5% is added through the end of December.
  • An additional 0.5% accrues effective January 1.
  • An additional 1% per month is added effective February 1.

The City Recorder's page uses the same November 1 to December 15 dates for real and personal property. The city's page links to an online lookup and payment tool.

sections.h2: When is the Maury County tax due, and how can you pay?
sections.html:
County tax can be paid from the first Monday of October through the last day of February. On March 1, county taxes become delinquent and a 1.5% penalty and interest charge starts, rising each month after that.

The Trustee accepts partial payments, and interest applies to all unpaid balances on March 1. The postmark date is honored, with one exception: it stops counting once delinquent taxes go to Chancery Court on April 1.

Payment options listed by Maury County are:

  • In person at One Public Square, 8 a.m. to 4 p.m.
  • Mail to Maury County Trustee, One Public Square, Columbia, TN 38401.
  • The after-hours drop box in front of the office, with no cash.
  • Online with a card or e-check, which carries a vendor fee of 2.5%, charged by the vendor and not by the county.
  • By phone at 1-877-556-4502.
  • Monthly ACH debits in equal installments; call 931-375-2201 to ask.

sections.h2: Is 2026 a reappraisal year in Columbia, and how do you appeal?
sections.html:
Yes. Maury County's Assessor page says reappraisals run every four years and that 2026 is the current reappraisal year. The appraised value on the Assessor's records reflects fair market value as of January 1 of the last reappraisal year, plus the equalized value of any improvements added since then.

The Assessor's page tells owners who feel the value is unfair that they may appeal to the local board of equalization and then to the State Board of Equalization. The state's calendar sets the county board's first meeting on June 1, and appeals to the State Board are due August 1 or within 45 days of the county board's notice, whichever is later. For 2026, the county board stage has passed, so a new challenge would apply to the next cycle.

sections.h2: What tax relief can Columbia homeowners apply for?
sections.html:
Columbia owners can apply for state relief, and seniors can also get a small city credit. The city provides up to $75 per year of additional relief to qualifying seniors, who must be 65 or older as of December 31 of the prior year and have household income of $38,470 or less.

The state program is not a separate state tax. It is state-funded help with local property taxes for qualifying seniors, completely and permanently disabled owners, disabled veterans and surviving spouses of disabled veterans. The same $38,470 income cap applies to seniors and disabled applicants, counting you, your spouse and everyone on the deed. Veterans and surviving spouses submit Form F-16 or F-16S with Department of Veterans Affairs documentation, and the City Recorder's Office at City Hall has the forms.

The application deadline for all of these is January 20 of the current year. The Trustee's office will also help qualifying elderly, disabled and veteran taxpayers with the state paperwork.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about Columbia itself?
sections.html:
Columbia serves as the seat of Maury County and sits in the Nashville metropolitan area. The Census Bureau counted 41,690 residents in April 2020 and estimates 50,072 for July 2025, a gain of 20.3% from its estimates base. The city's own 2024 special census reported 48,885.

The town was laid out in 1808 and incorporated in 1817 on the Duck River, at the southern edge of the Nashville Basin. It calls itself the mule capital of the world and holds Mule Day each April. Columbia State Community College is based here, Maury County Public Schools serves the city, and the James K. Polk Home draws visitors.

Census QuickFacts shows these 2020 to 2024 figures for Columbia:

  • Typical owner-occupied home value: $308,700.
  • Owner-occupied rate: 63.3%.
  • Median gross rent: $1,197.
  • Median household income: $63,719.
  • Households: 18,039.

sections.h2: How do you estimate a Columbia tax bill by hand?
sections.html:
Multiply the appraised value by the assessment ratio for the property's class, then multiply that result by the tax rate. The Maury County Assessor's page spells out this order, and residential property in Tennessee is assessed at 25%.

For a house at Columbia's Census median value of $308,700, the assessed value is $77,175. Divide by 100 and multiply by each rate: one for the county and one for the city. Ask the Maury County Trustee for the county rate and the City Recorder for the city rate on your parcel, since the rates change when the county commission and city adopt new budgets.

In a reappraisal year the appraisal itself changes too, so compare the new notice with last year's value before you assume the bill will match.

sections.h2: How does Columbia's climate and housing age affect a sale?
sections.html:
Rain and melted snow add up to about 57 inches in a typical Columbia year, per the NOAA normals Wikipedia reproduces, and the climate is humid subtropical. Summers are hot, with an average July high near 89 degrees, and winters are mild to cool, with only about an inch of snow in a year.

Buyers will want to see the current tax bill, so ask the Trustee and the City Recorder for written balances before you list. A delinquent county balance goes to Chancery Court on April 1, so clear it before then. A postmarked payment is honored up to that date.

faqs.q: When is Columbia, TN city property tax due?
faqs.a: City tax is due without penalty from November 1 through December 15. Because today is November 15, 2026, there is still a month to pay for this year. After December 15, 0.5% is added through December, another 0.5% from January 1 and 1% a month from February 1.

faqs.q: When does Maury County property tax become delinquent?
faqs.a: March 1. County tax can be paid from the first Monday of October through the last day of February, and interest of 1.5% applies from March 1, growing monthly. Delinquent accounts go to Chancery Court on April 1.

faqs.q: Do I pay both city and county tax in Columbia?
faqs.a: Yes. The City of Columbia says anyone living within the city limits must pay both city and county property taxes. The city bills its own tax, and the Maury County Trustee bills the county portion.

faqs.q: Is there property tax relief for seniors in Columbia?
faqs.a: Yes. Seniors 65 or older with income of $38,470 or less can apply for state relief, and the city adds up to $75 a year for qualifying seniors. Applications are due January 20 of the current year.

faqs.q: Which office answers questions about my Columbia home's value?
faqs.a: Call the Maury County Property Assessor at 931-375-4001 or visit 6 Public Square. Reappraisals are done every four years, and 2026 is the current reappraisal year in the county.
